thread:
sam: FYI started a tiny canary for peregrine-ptq-int6 on onboarding toolcall flows. Seeing JSON parse errors that look different than truncation — parsers complain about invalid UTF-8 byte sequences rather than EOF.

jia: example trace (raw chunk boundaries shown):
```
chunk1: {"action":"note","params":{"text":"User reported: \u00e2\u0080\u009cPayment failed
"
chunk2: \u009d","user":42}}
```
parser: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 14: invalid start byte

omar: interesting. Non-streaming replay of same prompts parse fine. looks like multi-byte UTF-8 sequences are being split across stream chunk boundaries and not reassembled properly before decode.

neha: do we see replacement chars (�) or explicit \uFFFD markers in logs? that would indicate decoder dropping malformed sequences.

sam: yes — some traces show the replacement char in chunk joins, others show raw broken byte escapes. batch size 3, streaming continuous-mode. float and int8 baselines have near-zero occurrences.

jia: short-term mitigations: 1) make streamer ensure chunk joins happen at UTF-8 codepoint boundaries (don't cut inside a multi-byte sequence) OR use chunk framing that includes byte-length, 2) client-side heuristic: try UTF-8 repair (replace-invalid-with-closest-equivalent) then parse for canary only, 3) allow a single internal retry forcing sync-mode for parse-fails and log repair_attempts.

omar: +1 on framing fix long-term. Short-term we can also detect invalid utf sequences earlier and treat chunk as incomplete until subsequent piece arrives (hold a 1-2ms buffer). add metric invalid_utf_chunk_count.

telemetry-bot: canary-deploy peregrine-ptq-int6 -> 2026-03-28T09:12:05Z (id: b7c9f)

eha: I'll wire metrics: invalid_utf_chunk_count, utf_repair_attempts, repair_success_rate, sync_retry_win_rate. dashboard tile in 20m.

sam: plan: 1) flip 12% of canary to sync-mode probe to confirm streaming-specific, 2) enable client utf-repair and single-sync retry for canary, 3) collect masked last-12-bytes for failures (PII scrub) to diagnose whether split happens at multibyte boundaries, 4) run 2k-prompt replay across float/int8/int6 and post diffs in 1h.

jia: if sync-mode removes errors that's strong signal for stream-chunk assembly bug. then we fix streamer framing and add unit tests for multibyte boundary handling.

omar: also check tokenizer step — if tokenizer outputs byte-level chunks we might need to ensure we transmit utf-8 canonical form. Could be an interaction with microquant attention kernel emitting chunks differently.

sam: good points. keeping canary small. ping infra to watch for correlated preemptions but this looks strictly chunk-assembly related so far. :mag:
